Authorization, storage, size and compilation failures are not suppressed.

Assignment example: `remnawave.assignments = [{hosts: ["RECIPIENT_HOST_UUID"], balancerTag: "auto-eu"}]`. Here hosts identifies recipients of the generated autoselect, not its pool members. Pool servers are selected separately in remnawave.injectHosts; auto-eu must match routing.balancers[].tag. The GUI calls this Where to use autoselect; editing JSON manually is optional.

The host edit form shows Saved JSON assignment: an explicit host template, assignment by host UUID, assignment by tag, or no explicit assignment. The template name opens its editor and the balancer appears beside it. Viewing is read-only. Unsaved tags and user-specific response overrides do not replace this saved assignment. Assigned profiles omit unused balancers and provably unused pools with explicit prefixes. Site-specific routing, fallback outbounds and geofile targets are preserved. Dynamic remark/tag names and unproven complex dependencies are retained. Balancer tags must be unique within one JSON configuration; separate profiles may reuse them.

random and roundRobin do not require an observer without fallbackTag. With a fallback configured, Xray uses observations to exclude unavailable servers; the editor preserves these checks. observatory and burstObservatory are alternatives. The former uses an interval and enableConcurrency; burst distributes probes over time and retains a sampling window. sampling is not simply requests per tick: a cycle relates to interval × sampling and affects failure detection and recovery. Burst does not guarantee lower traffic or indistinguishability. Existing observer type, URL, method and intervals are not replaced automatically. Select the mode in probe settings and measure through the client.

sections.title: Autoselect limits
sections.body: Quota and speed are configured on the recipient host. Autoselect does not debit pool members or inherit their speed limits. Multiple autoselects for one recipient share its allowance. Without recipient limits or enabled recipient tag limits, autoselect has no host-level ceiling. The account quota still applies. Xray JSON uses separate credentials for direct and autoselect connections. Direct access debits the member; autoselect debits only its recipient, with the recipient multiplier and enabled tag limits. User and device ceilings remain shared when switching members. Different recipients have independent limits. Access permissions, device bans, account status and destination restrictions still apply. Separate route accounting requires Node/Core with remnacust-routed-device-speed-v1; older components refuse routed policies. Update Node/Core before enabling it and refresh the subscription in the app. Old credentials retain their previous accounting; recorded history is not reassigned. If one host’s DENY overlaps a broader ALLOW_ONLY entry on the other, the overlapping allow entry is removed entirely.

sections.title: History and recovery
sections.body: Xray JSON, Singbox, Mihomo, Clash and Stash retain the last 30 saved versions. The database upgrade preserves existing code as the first version. History shows dates and a comparison with the current draft. Open in editor restores all code, including autoselect, balancers and assignments. Replacing an unsaved draft requires confirmation. Saving creates a new version, so a restore can itself be undone. An unsuccessful save changes neither code nor history.

sections.title: Autoselect in every editable format
sections.body: Autoselect is available for Xray JSON, sing-box, Mihomo, Clash and Stash. sing-box uses urltest/selector; YAML clients use url-test/select/fallback/load-balance. Groups can filter UUIDs, tags or regex with all/random/group and source visibility. Access is checked before selection; an empty explicit pool never becomes DIRECT. Manual members remain intact. Group name and default route are separate controls. All tabs share a draft; an unsaved Xray test pool can be removed with its dependent balancer. Forms show Save and Discard draft; code tools appear only in Editing.

sections.title: Geofiles library
sections.body: Ready-made datasets include published V2Fly and MetaCubeX GeoIP/GeoSite. Import uses the same HTTPS and content checks and never enables rules automatically. Use Click to upload for a local file. In Geofiles, upload from your computer or import a direct HTTPS URL, with a name and content format. Select a library item, attach it, select DAT categories and explicitly choose DIRECT, REJECT or a group. Multiple files and reuse across templates are supported. DAT becomes native rules on the server; sing-box JSON/SRS and Mihomo YAML/text use remote rule_set/rule-providers. Clash/Stash support YAML payload. Existing settings remain intact. Save the template and refresh the subscription to apply. File URLs are public: never upload secrets. Up to 32 files of 64 MiB, text up to 8 MiB; local addresses, archives and unrelated content are rejected. Preserve backups/geofiles when migrating: database-only backups exclude binary files. Historical versions may require reattachment after a file is deleted.

sections.title: Priority and backup servers
sections.body:
Priority: first available selects the first working server. For an exact order, choose Hosts and All selected hosts, then reorder them with the arrows. Multiple pool prefixes can also be reordered in the balancer. Tags and regex follow the main host list; random modes select a subset first. Failover and return to the primary follow health checks and affect new connections; existing connections are not migrated. Connections are blocked before the first successful probe and when every server is unavailable. An explicit fallbackTag is used last. Selecting priority in the GUI removes the generated fallback to the same pool and preserves custom fallbacks. Probe settings are preserved. Limits: 128 candidates per balancer and 256 per configuration. Routing scripts and conflicting broad selectors of other balancers are incompatible. Mihomo/Clash/Stash use native fallback in proxies order: explicit code members precede pool members. sing-box has no automatic strict priority mode in its configuration; selector is manual and URLTest uses latency. A full JSON/YAML subscription is required.

Use Server order to open the ordering dialog. Arrows move members and long lists are paginated. Select explicit hosts and all selected hosts for precise per-server order. Round robin rotates new connections; it does not retain the first server until failure. Use Priority: first available for failover. Explicit round-robin order is retained in the subscription, with up to 128 members per balancer and 256 per configuration. Save the template and refresh the subscription after changing the order.

sections.title: When to add the recipient host as proxy
sections.body: Also add the recipient host as proxy maps to remnawave.addVirtualHostAsOutbound. When enabled, the generator additionally builds a separate outbound tagged proxy from the recipient host’s address, port, transport and security settings. Autoselect does not require this switch; it does not enable TLS automatically. Leave it off for an Automatic placeholder representing a balancer. Real injectHosts pool members and the balancer remain in the configuration. Enable it only for a real additional connection supported by the client. A core may reject public VLESS without TLS/REALITY or VLESS encryption; Happ iOS proxy-based checks can report failed to build outbound config with tag proxy / vless without TLS. A successful ordinary test or another device does not validate this extra outbound. Disable the switch for a placeholder, or correct transport and security for a real host. Save the template and update the subscription in the app. The switch does not reconfigure servers or install certificates.

sections.title: Distribute connections
sections.body:
Choose Distribute connections to rotate new connections across available pool members. The client excludes servers that fail its HTTP check. This does not select by CPU, memory, user count or spare bandwidth. Existing long-lived connections keep their server, so equal numbers of new connections do not guarantee equal traffic volume.

Xray uses roundRobin with HTTP checks. Before initial probe results, availability is unknown and a member can still be selected. Traffic is blocked when probes show every member is unavailable and no custom fallback is configured. An explicit fallback outbound is preserved. Mihomo, Clash and Stash use load-balance with round-robin. sing-box has no round-robin distribution here: this choice explicitly uses urltest, selecting an available server by HTTP response time. Probe-site reachability affects selection. Save the template and refresh the subscription after changing strategy; the app then updates its probe results without downloading the subscription again.

sections.title: Temporary delivery errors
sections.body: A failed user, device or host query does not mean the subscription was deleted. Configuration delivery returns a temporary error asking the client to retry after 30 seconds; a genuinely missing user still returns 404. A failed host query is not reported as a successful empty subscription. If there truly are no available hosts, extra template and quota queries are skipped. For repeated failures, check the log and database connectivity; do not replace a user’s keys to solve a network error.

sections.title: Output size and generation errors
sections.body: A generated subscription is limited to 16 MiB. Sing-box, Mihomo, Stash and Clash group expansion is also bounded during generation with room for escaping and formatting; excessive fanout may be rejected before reaching the exact limit. Reduce the number of groups or their servers. Generation failures return HTTP 503 rather than an empty successful subscription. When the cache is unavailable, templates are read from the database.

sections.title: Saving with warnings
sections.body: Save remains available for invalid JSON/YAML, empty host selections and incomplete geofile actions. Text with errors is saved on the server as a draft and included in history; reopening restores the same text. Subscriptions keep the last working configuration. Fix the warnings and save again: valid content replaces the working version and clears the draft. Network and database failures are not reported as successful saves.

sections.title: Host selection and balancing in one card
sections.body: Host sources and their strategy share one block. Pools using a shared balancer are grouped together; manual balancers remain visible. Deleting the block removes its sources, balancers and linked rules while retaining independent groups and manual outbounds. leastLoad.expected is the selected node count; tolerance is the allowed failed probe fraction from 0 to 1: 0.01 means 1%, and 2 does not mean two nodes. Xray clamps finite numeric values outside the range to 0–1; such templates apply without a redundant warning while retaining the original number. Changing the strategy in the GUI removes the previous algorithm settings; reselecting leastLoad preserves its parameters. Host UUID hover shows localized parameters instead of technical JSON. New pools start with enabled hosts supported by the format, selected by UUID. With no eligible hosts, the setup remains a draft until sources are selected.

sections.title: Standard geofiles and Happ recovery
sections.body:
For automatic delivery, enable the geofile master switch and JSON at the base subscription URL, then enable geofiles for the required template. Full standard GeoSite and GeoIP datasets remain available alongside custom categories: ordinary names, including CATEGORY-RU, are retained, and custom categories receive separate names.

Set a 48-hour refresh interval and enable automatic updates for standard datasets. The interval can be changed per file. Update now checks the source immediately. If SHA-256 is unchanged, the active file is not replaced. After content changes, save the template if needed and refresh the subscription in the app.

If Happ cannot find a standard category after using custom files, refresh its subscription. With the geofile master switch enabled and full standard datasets available, the panel can restore the standard files, including after a panel restart. Explicit Routing settings and custom geodata retain priority. Manual geosite:, geoip: and ext: rules are preserved; restoring standard datasets does not require rewriting them.

sections.title: Public geofile path
sections.body:
Clients download geofiles over HTTPS from the subscription domain through /geofiles/. If the website uses a separate CUSTOM_SUB_PREFIX, root links and previously saved prefixed links remain supported together. Domain access rules apply to both addresses.

Forward GET and HEAD requests for /geofiles/* to the subscription website in your reverse proxy, even when other pages use a separate prefix. Check this route if downloads return 404. To verify delivery, download the DAT and its .sha256: the checksum must match the file. Refresh the subscription in the app after correcting the route.

sections.title: When the app downloads geofiles
sections.body: The panel measures each profile including list expansion and client formatting. Small datasets are inline rules; Happ/INCY download large datasets as DAT. A JSON subscription is required: enable “Serve JSON at the base subscription path” or use /json. Save the template and refresh the subscription.

sections.title: Host previews in the editor
sections.body: Hover over a host UUID in a JSON/YAML value to see its name, address, port, SNI, path, tags, state and profile assignment. Assignments, selector values and groups, host:UUID references and history comparisons are supported. Previews use the already loaded host list without requesting it on each hover. Deleted or unavailable hosts are not disclosed. Completion searches both UUID and name. Select and copy preview content; Escape closes it. Comments and property names are not references. To preserve responsiveness, hover parsing is limited to documents up to 2 MiB; long preview fields are shortened.

sections.title: Automatic geofile delivery and size
sections.body: With JSON enabled on the base link, Throne 1.x from stable 1.2.0 receives full Xray JSON arrays through its User-Agent. If a beta build is reported, support starts at 1.2.0-beta.5. Older or unrecognized versions keep their previous format. Explicit /json and /v2ray-json choose a configuration even with a browser User-Agent. This does not grant Throne special Happ/INCY extensions or DAT delivery; normal compatible-client rules and budgets apply. Explicit format choices and access denials remain effective. There is no manual delivery switch. All selected geofiles are first converted to inline rules. INCY receives long comma-free lists in lossless Xray StringList form. The configured condition threshold (20,000 by default) applies independently to each final profile. Only an oversized profile switches to DAT; other profiles retain inline rules. An independent 900,000-byte safety budget after four-space formatting and StringList expansion may apply earlier. The former 90 KB switching threshold has been removed. This is a panel compatibility reserve, not a documented exact application limit. Host profiles are not added together for this comparison. A separate 16 MiB full-response transport limit remains. If a profile is too large, supported Happ/INCY receive bundled DAT with isolated category names. Inline compilation limits can also trigger downloads. Other Xray clients receive up to 50,000 inline conditions across files in one template without Happ/INCY headers; the configurable threshold applies only to automatic DAT delivery. Under Geofiles → Shared inline rule threshold, enter 1–250,000 addresses/conditions (default 20,000). This is shared by all templates and counts entries, not JSON lines. Save and refresh the subscription; templates do not need to be saved again. Independent size limits may switch delivery earlier. Compilation, template-size and full-response bounds remain; rules are never truncated. The app must support full JSON configuration import. Server-link subscriptions do not carry routing. v2rayTun uses its own routing format, not a Happ/INCY profile. With JSON at the base address enabled, v2rayTun receives the full configuration with these rules. Host exclusions and an explicit JSON opt-out in response rules still apply. Small sing-box/Mihomo/Clash/Stash datasets are inline and large ones remote; binary SRS is always remote. Legacy Clash also downloads native providers for compatibility. DIRECT, REJECT, groups and routing order are preserved. Manual routing/geodata are not overwritten: incompatible oversized output fails explicitly. Profile names use the subscription profile-title, including squad overrides, or the subscription domain as fallback; a stable short suffix isolates identical names. Legacy downloadToClient is accepted but no longer chooses delivery. Client intervals apply only to remote delivery; server refresh has a separate schedule.

sections.title: Geofiles: enabling and disabling
sections.body: In Subscription settings → Additional options, enable JSON at the base path, then Remnacust geofile system. The master switch defaults to off, including after upgrading to this version. While off, template geofile icons and commands are hidden and API enabling is rejected. The library and saved assignments remain. Enable geofiles separately for each template using ⋯. Its icon shows the state; new templates default to off. The editor tab requires both the master and template switches. Turning the master off stops automatic rules and DAT delivery in every newly generated subscription format and pauses source schedules, retaining template preferences. Turn the master off before disabling base-path JSON. Disabling one template affects only that template. Explicit administrator-written geosite:, geoip:, ext:, geodata and routing headers remain unchanged in either state. A category reference does not download a file: configure manual source downloads and updates separately in a compatible app. Manual library operations remain available while the system is off. Refresh the subscription in the app after changing settings. In-flight requests may finish using earlier settings; previously issued signed URLs remain valid.

sections.title: Startup and concurrent requests
sections.body: After panel startup, the first subscription using geofiles may take longer to prepare. When many requests arrive, allow preparation to finish and retry. A 503 response with Retry-After: 2 means waiting at least two seconds before the next attempt. The subscription page waits up to 30 seconds for the panel. For an access error, check permissions and the page connection to the panel.

sections.title: Removing a geofile from a template
sections.body: Save the template and refresh the subscription in the app. If this subscription previously received our DAT files, disabling all custom files or returning all its profiles to inline rules replaces their sources with standard GeoIP/GeoSite from Loyalsoldier/v2ray-rules-dat, using the addresses documented by Happ and INCY. An empty URL alone does not restore a saved DAT. The panel keeps the previously issued profile name, advances its revision, clears only its additional rule lists and disables file trimming and scheduled downloads. The app must successfully download the standard files; reconnect the VPN afterwards. This does not restore the exact bundled files of a particular app version. Recovery remains incomplete if the download fails. Manual geosite:/geoip: rules in JSON remain unchanged. An explicit routing header or manual geodata section takes precedence: the panel does not replace those sources. A fresh subscription without managed-file history receives no download instruction. Recovery requires retained server history for that profile and device; if it is lost or the name changes, restore standard geofiles using the app. Standard sources never replace a managed DAT while any subscription profile still uses it. Removing one of several files of the same kind leaves only the remaining sources in the combined DAT; URLs and lists for a removed kind are cleared. Other app profiles and the library are preserved. Changed DAT content receives a new signed address; unchanged content keeps its address. Previously issued links and .sha256 checks remain valid.

sections.title: GeoIP for domain destinations
sections.body: When geofiles generate GeoIP rules, the final Xray JSON uses IPOnDemand: DNS resolution occurs when an IP rule is reached. DIRECT, REJECT and GeoIP balancers can then match before the TCP/UDP catch-all. Inline rules and downloaded DAT use the same behavior. Earlier manual rules retain priority and the source template is not overwritten. Domain-only GeoSite and other client formats keep their DNS strategy. If resolution fails, subsequent routing rules apply.

sections.body: With JSON enabled on the base link, Throne 1.x from stable 1.2.0 receives full Xray JSON arrays through its User-Agent. If a beta build is reported, support starts at 1.2.0-beta.5.
